sources.entry: Events As First-Class Citizens - By Randy Shoup, January 2018. Focusses on the most important part of EDA: The actual events.

summary.title: Events As First-Class Citizens
summary.one_liner: Events should be treated as a core building block of software design, since they decouple services and provide a durable record of state changes, illustrated with Stitch Fix's fix-lifecycle workflow.
keywords: how to model workflow with events
takeaways: Model a multi-step workflow as a state machine where each step emits an event marking a state transition.
Events decouple producers from consumers: producers publish without knowing who subscribes, so consumers can be added, removed or scaled freely.
Recording every event gives a history of what happened and when, useful for support, analytics and debugging.
Event sourcing rebuilds current state by replaying stored events, similar to double-entry bookkeeping.
Eventual consistency and asynchrony feel less foreign when you think of familiar workflows like code moving from commit to production.
summary.summary: Randy Shoup, writing in January 2018, argues that events deserve to be treated as a fourth fundamental building block alongside presentation, application and persistence. He uses the lifecycle of a clothing "fix" at Stitch Fix, modeled as a state machine whose transitions emit events, to show how services produce and consume events. He then covers event-based decoupling, using events as an audit record (linking to event sourcing), and compares asynchronous workflows to a everyday software development pipeline. The post ends with a list of further resources such as talks on microservices and event sourcing and Enterprise Integration Patterns.
